replace.grasp_plan:
Generate inspectable public RGB-D grasp candidates for one current target.
Use when: current grounding or segmentation identifies the intended object and you need parallel-jaw poses. Select the arm on dual-arm embodiments.
Effect: read-only; queries Contact-GraspNet using the selected source-camera RGB-D and compiles poses to the public TCP convention. ALOHA also supplies geometry-derived top-down candidates. Optional synchronized views provide review evidence.
Returns: up to three candidates, complete world-frame pregrasp_pose and contact_pose, copyable bounded contact_approach targets, predicted opening, compiler checks and labeled review images. Reachability is delegated to move_pose. Inspect every candidate panel and choose target identity and geometry independently of rank. After choosing a current candidate, use grasp_execute(candidate_id, rationale) when you accept its committed approach/close/verify sequence without intermediate decisions. Choose manual move_pose plus set_gripper when you need a separate observation or decision before closing. Choose this path before moving: any world action stales the candidate, so call grasp_plan again before later using grasp_execute. Pose handoff: when manually commanding a returned world pose, set position_mode=absolute and orientation_mode=absolute_quaternion, then copy position_m and orientation_xyzw unchanged. Put these fields under targets.<selected_arm>. Choose interaction by the intended physical contact. Schema example only; replace the illustrative pose and arm with your selected current result:
{"tool":"move_pose","arguments":{"targets":{"right":{"position_mode":"absolute","position_m":[0.1,0.0,0.9],"orientation_mode":"absolute_quaternion","orientation_xyzw":[0.0,0.0,0.0,1.0],"interaction":"precision"}}}}
Does not: plan trajectories, certify reachability, move the robot, command a gripper, use object ground truth, certify retention or report task success. Backend rank is not a success probability. Missing optional review cameras do not invalidate usable primary input.
On error: obtain a better current view or select another target or candidate. Recompute after the target or observation changes. After a submitted motion fails, use its phase and measured residual to choose the next action. Retention evidence remains advisory.
replace.place_plan:
Propose a bounded, numeric next placement step from selected current public RGB-D regions.
Use when: explicitly select the arm that holds or released this object; a retained object is near a visible destination and you need a preplace, lower, or short exit candidate. Select object_ref, then name the destination as flat fields: destination_kind, destination_support_ref, and destination_boundary_ref for open_container or front_cavity, which is refused by name when it is missing there and when it is supplied for support_surface. A whole-container centroid is not its cavity. Re-localize after every physical action.
Effect: read-only with respect to the world; creates an immutable observation-bound assessment, measured geometry and overlay. It consumes no robot decision, executes no motion and changes no action admission state. The original mask and depth are preserved as immutable evidence. In this placement-only projection, boundary discontinuity pixels are flagged uncertain, not certified background; the original depth remains available for inspection.
Returns: candidates, no_candidate or unknown with at most three one-step world-pose candidates, checks, stage evidence and hashed public evidence. For a current phase=lower candidate, use place_execute(candidate_id, rationale) when you accept the committed transport/descend/release/settle sequence. Set stop_before_commit=true if you need a fresh view before release; after status=stopped, use place_resume to continue or abandon. For preplace/exit candidates, or when you need separate decisions at other stages, use manual move_pose and set_gripper. After any world action, obtain current evidence and re-plan before selecting another candidate. Pose handoff: when manually commanding a returned world pose, set position_mode=absolute and orientation_mode=absolute_quaternion, then copy position_m and orientation_xyzw unchanged. Put these fields under targets.<selected_arm>. Choose interaction by the intended physical contact. Schema example only; replace the illustrative pose and arm with your selected current result:
{"tool":"move_pose","arguments":{"targets":{"right":{"position_mode":"absolute","position_m":[0.1,0.0,0.9],"orientation_mode":"absolute_quaternion","orientation_xyzw":[0.0,0.0,0.0,1.0],"interaction":"precision"}}}}
assessment_ref is an audit reference, never an executable trajectory. Inspect the reported depth-edge uncertainty: all retained points still face unchanged support/opening tests. When boundary evidence is unresolved, candidates are conditional on unresolved silhouette, not full-object fit, passage or release certificates.
Does not: prove object identity, grasp attachment, stable support, physical release or official success; infer hidden cavity volume; or certify a collision-free scene/payload trajectory. The existing RoboTwin motion route is unchanged; this tool adds no scene or carried-object collision model. No visible conflict is not collision-free. upright uses a fit to the selected visible circular rim, not a PCA cup axis; absent/invalid rim evidence stays unknown. Each protected_before_refs and protected_current_refs entry at the same index is an Agent association, not identity authentication. A boundary depth gap cannot distinguish leaked background from a true farther surface or thin handle; flagged pixels remain unresolved evidence, not semantic background exclusions.
On error: inspect fresh complementary RGB-D and reselect functional regions; do not replace missing geometry with a guessed center or stale candidate. Retention checks supply advisory geometric evidence; decide closed-gripper motion from fresh observations and the reported uncertainty. For manual placement, inspect before release, release as a separate action, inspect after release and inspect again after a short departure. With place_execute, these steps belong to its committed stages; the optional pre-release stop is the available intermediate decision point. Use place_resume(abandon) before choosing a different placement. Each check is evidence for Agent judgment, not an automatic release or success authorization.
Arm binding: every gripper command, retention check and placement check must name the intended arm, whichever calls this surface advertises for them. Opposite-arm opening does not release this object; opposite-arm motion is not this arm's exit. All candidates stale after any world action, including motion of the other arm. A successful gripper receipt says executed, not Cartesian reached; it is command completion, not physical release. geometry_status and measured checks are separate from stage_evidence and uncertainty_reasons. Unconfirmed action stage preserves valid geometric candidates; inspect their prerequisites and decide subsequent actions independently.
replace.set_gripper:
Set one or both grippers to a named directive in a single call.
Use when: you are opening to release or approach, or closing to grasp, and you already know which directive each gripper should hold. On a two-armed embodiment this is how the two are coordinated: naming both in one call is the only way to state that they change together. Near miss: this is not grasp_execute. If you have chosen a current grasp candidate and accept the committed sequence without intermediate decisions, call that instead -- it approaches, closes and measures as one committed sequence, and a bare close here does none of that. Use this standalone command when a separate decision after pose execution is needed.
Effect: submits one gripper directive per named gripper through the Supervisor and consumes one robot decision. **An omitted gripper holds its current directive; it is not re-sent and not re-actuated.** The end-effector pose target is held unchanged. Measured state may still move under contact, and that is evidence rather than a fault.
Returns: a submitted acknowledgement, then a measured receipt and a fresh observation on the next turn. When closing, an intent block echoes the target_ref you supplied and labels it agent_annotation_only.
Does not: prove anything was grasped, held, released or moved; report jaw separation; verify what the jaws closed on; or make target_ref evidence -- it is your annotation of what you believe you are closing on, never a measurement. A closed jaw is not a grasp.
On error: invalid_motion_arguments names the field that was wrong -- re-read this schema rather than resubmitting the same shape. invalid_arguments naming target_ref means a blank string was sent; send a non-empty reference or omit it entirely.
